text.en: Meena read that every child has a right to education. "Who gave us rights?" she asked.

Human rights are the basic rights every person has simply by being human, such as life, liberty and equality. The United Nations adopted the Universal Declaration of Human Rights on 10 December 1948, and we mark it as Human Rights Day.
In India the Constitution gives Fundamental Rights, including equality, freedom, protection against exploitation, freedom of religion, cultural and educational rights and the right to constitutional remedies. Children also have rights to education and protection.
Rights come with duties. The National and State Human Rights Commissions look into violations, and courts protect rights.

problem.en: Why do rights come with duties?

text.en: My rights depend on others respecting them.
I must respect others' rights too.

prompt.en: A friend says Human rights were declared by India in 1948. How will you reply?

points.en: Fundamental Rights are in the Constitution.
